description: The commandmate CLI subcommands and options the cmate-orchestrate runners are allowed to use, transcribed verbatim from `commandmate <cmd> --help` (CommandMate 0.17.0). The fake CLI enforces this surface and the contract-parity test asserts the runners only ever call subcommands/flags listed here — so a runner that reaches for a non-existent flag (the #1467 regression) fails the suite instead of only failing in production. When a real `commandmate` binary is on PATH the parity test additionally checks these flags are a subset of the live `--help`.
flag_values: `flag_values` closes a flag whose argument is an ENUM rather than free text. `send --duration` is the only one so far (Issue #136): CommandMate's DURATION_MAP accepts 1h / 3h / 8h and nothing else, and an unlisted value makes the CLI print "Error: Invalid duration" and exit BEFORE it sends anything — so a runner that computed a duration in seconds would abort the dispatch, not merely widen a window. The fake CLI refuses an unlisted value the same way, and the live `--help` check asserts the real binary still lists exactly these.
version_gating: `since` marks a subcommand, and `since_flags` marks individual flags, that a specific CommandMate version introduced (Issue #1588: the execution contract and the contract verdict both arrived in 0.17.0; Issue #91: `sync`, the server-side worktree re-scan, arrived in 0.21.0). The live `--help` parity check skips those entries when the installed binary predates them, and says out loud which ones it skipped — an older CLI legitimately does not list them, and asserting anyway would report a supported fallback as a contract drift. Entries with no `since` are asserted against every version.
capture_fields_note: The `capture --json` fields the dispatch runner reads before a worker's first send (CommandMate#3007), from CommandMate `src/cli/types/api-responses.ts` / `src/lib/session/current-output-builder.ts`: `isPromptWaiting` (a prompt the server can answer — the same answer the send guard of #1708 uses) and `isSelectionListActive` (`status === 'waiting'` with a selection-list reason: an unreadable question UI, Command Code's plan review — screens the send guard deliberately lets through). Either one true means a human has to decide on that screen. `interrupt` (0.28.0+) is the GUI's interrupt button; exit 30 means no session was running and nothing was interrupted.
send_failures_note: How `commandmate send` reports the refusals the runners branch on (CommandMate#3006), transcribed from CommandMate `src/cli/commands/send.ts` + `src/cli/utils/api-client.ts` handleApiError + `src/app/api/worktrees/[id]/send/route.ts`. A 5xx reaches stderr as `Error: Server error: <the server's error>` and exits 99; a 409 other than PROMPT_WAITING has no sentence of its own (`Unexpected HTTP status: 409`) and also exits 99; PROMPT_WAITING is the one refusal send.ts maps itself, to exit 2. `retry` is the runners' reading: only the two not-ready refusals typed nothing because the session had not started yet, so only those are re-sent (once). The fake CLI prints exactly these lines.

session_starting.stderr: Error: Server error: Command Code did not reach its input prompt within 30s (initialization timeout). The tmux session 'mcbd-command-code-<worktree-id>' and its process are still running, so this is a slow start, not a failed one — the message was not delivered, but nothing needs repairing. Retry the send in a few seconds, or run `commandmate capture <worktree-id>` to see what it is waiting on.

prompt_not_ready.stderr: Error: Server error: Command Code prompt not ready: timed out waiting for the composer before sending

prompt_waiting.stderr: Error: <worktree-id> is waiting on a prompt. Sending now would type into the prompt's input line instead of reaching the agent, and would leave that text in place for the next answer. Answer the prompt first: `commandmate respond <worktree-id> <answer>`.
